extensions.bf16: bfloat16: VXM element type code 16 and MXM weight type 4; legal in a profile whose `extensions` names it, an implementation choice (microarchitecture.md sec. 5)
extensions.wide_acc: wide accumulator: ACC type x128 (code 0); legal in a profile whose `extensions` names it together with mxm.acc_bits 128 (an implementation choice; see mxm.acc_bits)
extensions.block_fp8: block-scaled fp8: MXM weight type bfp8 (code 5); legal in a profile whose `extensions` names it (an implementation choice; see block_fp8_format)

decode_rule.text: Applied to the text of one queue, at the first unit of an instruction (model/postlude/iq.sail decode_text): (1) clear bit 31, the bundle bit. (2) tag = bits 30..28 of the unit: a narrow tag decodes the unit's bits 31..0 (bit 31 clear) against the width-32 entries; a wide tag takes the next unit of the queue's text as bits 31..0 and decodes the 64-bit word (unit 0 bits 30..0 as bits 62..32) against the width-64 entries; tag 6 or 7 is OTS-E-DEC-003 and consumes one unit. A word decodes to the one entry whose match pattern it matches and whose fields are all legal (field_rule); no such entry is OTS-E-DEC-003. The queue does not matter. Placement is checked after decoding: control_channel, then units (OTS-E-QUE-002).

text_format.text: The text of a queue is a sequence of 32-bit units. Parcel: the instructions between two units with bundle bit 0 (inclusive); a parcel is dispatched all at once. A unit with tag 0, opcode 0 and bundle bit 0 at the start of a parcel is a NOP n (n = bits 15..0, 1..65535): not an instruction but a timing prefix: the next parcel's earliest dispatch cycle is the cycle after the previous parcel's, plus the sum of the NOP counts before it (the first parcel: cycle 0, then plus the NOPs). The unit 0xFFFFFFFF is padding and is never enqueued. A queue's initial text (the harness `Q` lines, the object's images) is at most icu.iq_depth / 4 units. Fetched text (Ifetch, IfetchM) is 2 x vlanes bytes per instruction, appended to the target queue's text at icu.fetch_bytes_per_cycle starting icu.fetch_latency cycles after the fetch. `lowering` is the normative function from a cycle view to text.

nop.at: start of a parcel, bundle bit 0

lowering.text: lower(entries): entries are (cycle, queue, 64-bit word). Per queue sort by cycle (source order within a cycle). A NOP entry alone in its cycle makes no parcel (the gap NOPs carry the time). For each cycle with entries, let g = cycle - previous cycle - 1 (previous = -1 before the first): emit NOP units for g (each at most 65535, none for g = 0), then the entries' units, bundle bit 1 on the first unit of every entry but the last. An entry lowers to one unit when bits 63..32 are zero and bits 31..28 are a narrow tag, to two units (high half, low half) when bits 63..60 are a wide tag, else to the unit 0x6FFFFFFF (tag 6).

field_rule.text: A field value x (the bits at location, with the bits at hi_location above them and then the bits at top_location above those, when present: x = word[location] | word[hi_location] << width(location) | word[top_location] << (width(location) + width(hi_location))) is legal when every key present holds: codes / values: x is listed, and when x is listed in extension_codes[e] the profile's `extensions` names e; not_values: x is not listed; min / max: the value is in range, read as two's complement when the kind is signed and as unsigned otherwise; max_expr: x <= the expression, evaluated with profile_variables (for a signed kind the expression bounds the magnitude: -e <= x <= e); bool_values: when the entry's `type` field is one of boolean_codes, x is listed there; a `name` kind: x has a name in its table. Bit ranges are written `msb-lsb` (a single bit `n`), bit 0 is the least significant bit, match patterns are MSB first.

stream_encoding.text: A stream field holds 6 bits: bit 5 is the row (E = 0, W = 1), bits 4..0 the stream id 0..31 (topology.md sec. 4). A kind with `group` g holds (32 * row + id) / g, and id must be a multiple of g; stream_group16 is 2 bits: E:0 = 0, E:16 = 1, W:0 = 2, W:16 = 3.

acc_depth.meaning: the accumulators of an MXM plane (config/<profile>.json); the ACC index is below it

sram_words.meaning: the words a slice can address (config/<profile>.json: 8192 on ref); sram.words_per_slice is at most this

vlanes.meaning: the configured lane count (config/<profile>.json); SetVL does not change it

agt.text: AGT placement (microarchitecture.md sec. 4, model/postlude/tick.sail): each dispatch path (R, W) of a MEM queue has its own AGT. A loopable reference that dispatches alone on its path (no other reference on that path in that cycle) opens that path's configuration. A configuration record in the next cycle continues it; a cycle of the queue without a configuration record ends every open configuration. Configuration records carry no path: one goes to the configuring path, and when both are configuring (a Read + Write pair) to the one with fewer configuration records so far, R on a tie, so a pair's records alternate R, W. Within a level the fields go in `config` order; a field at or before the last one written starts the next level; a fifth level, or a configuration record with no open configuration (including one in the same cycle as its reference), is OTS-E-OPR-001 at run time.

mem_slots.text: Instructions per parcel (microarchitecture.md sec. 3, model/postlude/tick.sail place/classify). A queue of `units` takes, per parcel, instructions whose slots (`slot_of`) are all distinct: one Ifetch or IfetchM (slot fetch), per liquid thread one R-type reference (slot R) and one W-type reference (slot W), the slots in `per_thread` being keyed by the record's `thread` field, and one AGT configuration record (slot config). An instruction not in `slot_of` needs the whole queue and dispatches only alone. On any other queue a parcel holds one instruction. When a parcel's instructions do not fit (two in one slot, a whole-queue instruction with another, an instruction that does not decode among several), every instruction of that parcel is OTS-E-QUE-001. Bank rule (OTS-E-MEM-001 on both): an R and a W reference of the same thread in one cycle clash when they address the same bank (address bit sram.bank_bit), or when either is in `indirect` (its banks are unknown at dispatch); a word outside the slice (address >= sram.words_per_slice) addresses no bank and clashes with nothing; references of different threads never clash. An instruction in `all_threads` takes its per-thread slots on every thread, and its words (`sram_access`) clash by bank with a W reference of any thread (IfetchM, microarchitecture.md sec. 3).

sram_access.text: Words accessed from an sram_addr operand: a .. a + words - 1 (IfetchM: a and a + 1, microarchitecture.md sec. 3); an instruction not listed accesses one word. A symbol operand needs every accessed word inside its extern (OTS-E-ASM-002).

stations.text: Per unit (the names of `units`) and stream row, the gap at which the unit reads and writes (model/core/layout.sail; topology.md sec. 4). An expression is a configuration key, optionally '- quad' or '+ quad' with quad = (queue mod 44) div 4 for MEM; null: the unit cannot read (write) that row, and an operand there is OTS-E-DIR-001. A value outside 0..43 also means no station, and so does a MEM slice s with (s mod 44) >= geometry.mem_slices_per_hemisphere (an absent slice). A unit at gap g reads register g and writes register g + 1. C2C RX reads only for Ifetch.

control_channel.text: The control channel's text decodes like a data queue's; a decoded instruction not listed here is OTS-E-QUE-002 (model/postlude/tick.sail control).

units.text: The data queues of each unit name used in instructions[].units; `any` is every data queue 0..143 (not the control channel). An instruction on a data queue outside its units is OTS-E-QUE-002, and so is every instruction on the queue of an absent MEM slice ((queue mod 44) >= geometry.mem_slices_per_hemisphere).

queues.text: Canonical queue names (assembly.md sec. 3); aliases are accepted on input, never printed. An index may carry leading zeros (MEM[007] = MEM[7]); any other name is OTS-E-ASM-005.

diagnostics.OTS-E-DEC-003: does not decode (unknown opcode or slice tag 6, 7, reserved bit set, illegal type/mode)
diagnostics.OTS-E-QUE-001: a parcel that breaks the slot rule (each of its instructions)
diagnostics.OTS-E-QUE-002: instruction issued on a queue whose unit lacks it
diagnostics.OTS-E-TIM-001: no value at the reader's gap in the read cycle
diagnostics.OTS-E-DIR-001: the stream's only writers are at or downstream of the reader
diagnostics.OTS-E-SRF-002: two writes to one row/stream/gap in one cycle
diagnostics.OTS-E-MEM-001: a Read and a Write dispatched together hit the same bank
diagnostics.OTS-E-OPR-001: operand value out of range (for a Gather or Scatter tile address and an sxselect sel, per tile or lane: the good ones still take effect)
diagnostics.OTS-E-OPR-002: multi-stream operand not aligned to its width
diagnostics.OTS-E-RES-001: MXM state, or a Permute's SXM map, used before it is ready
diagnostics.OTS-E-RES-003: two instructions change one unit-state part in one cycle
diagnostics.OTS-E-SXM-001: Permute map is not bijective (a source lane repeats)
diagnostics.OTS-E-LNK-001: Send or Transmit on a link that accepted a vector fewer than c2c.cycles_per_vector cycles ago
diagnostics.OTS-E-LNK-002: a vector arrived at a link whose receive FIFO holds c2c.rx_depth vectors and was dropped (reported by the harness)
diagnostics.OTS-E-LNK-003: Send or Transmit released into the cycles of a csr or ctrl packet in flight on the link
diagnostics.OTS-E-IQ-002: fetched text arrived at a full IQ and the units that did not fit were lost (once per queue and cycle, by Enqueue)
diagnostics.OTS-E-IQ-003: an Ifetch or IfetchM found the queue's fetch staging FIFO holding icu.fetch_staging_depth payloads: it fetched nothing
diagnostics.OTS-E-IQ-004: text was left in an IQ at the end of the run that never completes a parcel (reported once per queue after the last cycle)
diagnostics.OTS-E-HIO-001: PciSend within host.cycles_per_vector cycles of the previous one
diagnostics.OTS-E-ECC-001: a stream operand had an uncorrectable (multi-bit) error in some superlane; reported once, after the instruction's own checks
diagnostics.OTS-E-LNK-004: a Receive took a vector whose link transfer had an uncorrectable (detected, not corrected) FEC error; the vector is written, its bad superlanes poisoned
diagnostics.OTS-E-ECC-003: the sum check of an ABC found an error it cannot correct; the ABC has no effect (microarchitecture.md sec. 18)
diagnostics.OTS-E-ECC-002: a text word of the instruction had an uncorrectable (multi-bit) error: the instruction consumes its units and has no effect
